findings.title: Tab III re-mapped variants are scored against text projected with a different PCA basis
findings.where: usplat/ablation_rows.py:92-96; scripts/eval_seg.py:256,281; usplat/feature_pca.py:32-34; scripts/run_mapping.py:161-169; scripts/replica_tab3.sh:110-113
findings.problem: Each re-mapped variant (pixels, centre, legacy) is a separate run_mapping.py run, so it fits its own PCA basis. run_mapping.py never seeds torch, and StreamingPCA.accumulate keeps a random 20,000 of the 76,800 pixels per frame (unseeded torch.randperm). ablation_rows.row_factory loads only ck['field'] from the variant file and ignores ck['pca']. eval_seg.load_scene projects the text with the MAIN field's basis (line 256 from_state(ckpt['pca']), line 281 project_text). So the variant's mu* (64-d coordinates in its own basis) is dotted with text in another basis. Nothing checks that the two bases are equal.
findings.failure_scenario: The Tab III rows 'Pixels instead of views', 'Centered features' and 'Pixel-level variant' change the PCA basis as well as the part they claim to change. Columns whose sign flips or that rotate between the two fits get the wrong sign in the class score, so mIoU/ECE/NLL of these rows drop for a reason unrelated to the ablation. 'Centered features' P0 should equal Full P0 exactly (same raw channel), but it will not.
findings.evidence: CPU proxy with the cached OpenCLIP tokens (not LSeg; GPU was off limits): two StreamingPCA fits on the same 20 Sequence_1 frames at 240x320 that differ only in the random subsample (scratchpad/pca_flip_idx.py, pca_cross_basis.py). office_0 seed 1 vs 2: 2 columns flip sign (57, 61). room_2 seed 1 vs 4: 7 columns flip (17, 19, 20, 41, 48, 60, 62) and 2 rotate. Accuracy of basis-B features scored with basis-B text vs basis-A text: office_0 0.6763 vs 0.6750; room_2 (seed 4) 0.7598 vs 0.7494 (-1.0 pt); room_2 (seed 5) 0.7597 vs 0.7568. CPU default generator is seeded differently per process (torch.initial_seed() printed 963274053633879740 then 14930468800794558177). PyTorch also seeds the CUDA default generator non-deterministically via getNonDeterministicRandom(is_cuda) (c10/core/GeneratorImpl.h:108), not confirmed on GPU. Partial val log shows Tab I row differences of about 0.1 pt mIoU, so a basis effect up to 1 pt is as large as the effects Tab III measures.
findings.fix: Make the basis identical by construction. Add run_mapping.py --pca-from <main field>, which loads its pca basis (and zbar) and skips the fit, and use it in replica_tab3.sh (and replica_views.sh for the k-view fields). In ablation_rows.row_factory, raise unless torch.equal(ck['pca']['basis'], main ckpt['pca']['basis']). Also seed run_mapping (torch.manual_seed, or pass a torch.Generator to accumulate).

findings.title: No pipeline produces the Tab III AUSE columns defined in the caption (e_red / e_irr averaged over 10/30/90-frame fields)
findings.where: papers/main.tex Table III caption (tab:ablation); usplat/ablation_rows.py:3-5; scripts/replica_tab3.sh:103-128; scripts/replica_views.sh:52-60; scripts/eval_views.py:98-109; usplat/seg_eval.py:381-384
findings.problem: replica_tab3.sh builds only full-length variant fields and runs eval_seg.py. eval_seg's 'ranking' AUSE uses err = 1 - correct on the full map (seg_eval.py:381), i.e. AUSE against the 0/1 error, not against e_red or e_irr. The ablation_rows docstring says its P0 rows supply 'the AUSE columns'. No script builds k-view fields for any variant. replica_views.sh hard-codes --row-factory usplat.baselines:row_factory and --rows ours_P0,ours_P2,averaging,normlift,viewcount, and deletes the k-view fields after each scene. eval_views.summarize reports per k; no code averages over k.
findings.failure_scenario: If the Tab III test run goes ahead as scripted, the only AUSE numbers for the variant rows are AUSE vs the 0/1 error on the 179-frame maps, which would be wrong under the caption's heading. Computing the captioned quantity afterwards needs new k-view mappings (3 variants x 3 k x 6 test scenes) and a second pass over the test scenes; the views run would already have deleted the main k-view fields the read-out rows could reuse.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'abl_|ablation_rows|views_test|e_red' over scripts/ and usplat/ finds no consumer combining ablation rows with k-view fields. replica_views.sh:53 fixes the baselines factory; line 60 does rm -f of the k fields. replica_tab3.sh:118 runs eval_seg with the ablation factory on full fields only. eval_views.py:98-109 summarizes per k.
findings.fix: Decide before the Tab III test. Either (a) extend replica_views.sh: map k-view fields per re-mapped variant (<s>_lseg_k<k>_<v>.pt, with the main PCA), use a row factory returning baseline plus ablation rows, pass betas merged from the Tab I and Tab III val fits, and add a step averaging AUSE(u_epi, e_red) and AUSE(u_ale, e_irr) over k per scene then over scenes, before the k fields are deleted. Or (b) change the caption and text to the quantity the pipeline measures (AUSE vs the 0/1 error on the full map).

findings.title: AUSE of u_ale ranks undefined (low-support) pixels as most uncertain, so it largely scores the tau_min gate; baseline channels get no such tier and the paper does not state the rule
findings.where: usplat/seg_eval.py:335-362 (undefined_key, ranking_signals), 382-384 (summarize); scripts/make_tables.py:22-28 (ours AUSE_u = u_ale; NormLift 1-R, 1-C_inter and CSS css_var_top always finite); papers/main.tex:680-682 (sec:metrics), :727-729 (Table I caption), :877-880 (Table III caption); fig:views text
findings.problem: Every AUSE of an own channel ranks pixels in 3 tiers: uncovered (+inf), then undefined (NaN), then finite values. u_ale is undefined when more than half a pixel's alpha comes from Gaussians with support < tau_min = 3 weighted views. That tier is a few-views (epistemic) signal entering ours' 'aleatoric' column; the baseline channels are finite everywhere and never get it. Defined u_ale values are tiny and flat, so the NaN tier may carry much of ours' ranking. The paper states the most-uncertain rule only for uncovered pixels. The same tier feeds the u_ale vs e_irr panel of Fig. views and the Table III 'ale' column. The per-pixel arrays are not saved, so a gate-free AUSE cannot be computed after the test run.
findings.failure_scenario: Ours' AUSE_u beats 1-C_inter or the CSS variance partly because of which pixels have fewer than 3 weighted views, not because rho_hat is better; the table and text would credit the estimator. Synthetic test through the real summarize() path with pure-noise u_ale: 10% undefined pixels give ours 15.60 vs an always-defined noise channel 17.53 (random gap 17.56), a 2-point 'win' from the gate alone. At M=10, u_ale is defined for only ~3.6% (office_0) / 7.0% (room_2) of pixel mass, so almost every covered pixel falls into one tied block and the u_ale curve says nothing about rho_hat; the rbar/joint/legacy Table III rows share the gate and are diluted toward the same value, while the 'pixels' variant gates differently. Because the low-support block is mostly reducible error, the gate can make u_ale appear to rank e_red, confounding the separation claim. A reader cannot reproduce ours' AUSE_u without knowing ~16-18% of covered pixels are ranked most uncertain.
findings.evidence: seg_eval.py:357/360: key = torch.where(isfinite(u), u, undefined_key(u)) (NaN ranks above max finite u); summarize() uses only this key (seg_eval.py:383); no defined-only variant (undefined="drop" only in evaluation.py). scratchpad/tiers.py on saved fields: office_0 'u_ale undefined 0.158 | 1-C_inter == 0 5.1e-07', defined q50/q90/q99/max = 0.017/0.043/0.058/0.101; room_2 'undefined 0.182 | 1.7e-06', 0.003/0.019/0.039/0.089 (consistent with logs/support_stats.log: u_ale defined for 84.2% / 81.8% of pixel mass; README: defined for 22.4% / 12.2% of Gaussians). CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" PYTHONPATH=. python3 scratchpad/ause_gate.py -> 'full map (M=180): undefined 10% | 3-tier 15.60 | defined only 15.92 | noise always defined 17.53 | random gap 17.56'; 'M=30: 60% | 18.35 | 17.43 | 23.59 | 23.57'; 'M=10: 95% | 24.74 | 17.39 | 26.80 | 26.72'. python3 scratchpad/gate_share.py -> office_0 pixel-mass defined M=10 3.6%, M=30 34.5%, M=90 69.7%, M=179 84.2%; room_2 7.0%, 39.3%, 69.7%, 81.8%.
findings.fix: Decide before the test run. (a) In summarize(), also compute each own channel's AUSE on one shared pixel set (covered pixels where our u_ale is defined, same set for CSS/NormLift), or give the baseline channels the same undefined treatment (NormLift N_eff or CSS support below the same threshold), or save per-pixel arrays (correct, covered, u channels, conf) of the test scenes. (b) State in sec:metrics and the Table I / Table III / Fig. views captions that a covered pixel with undefined u_ale ranks above every defined value (after uncovered), and print the undefined share (ranking[...]['n_undefined'] already in the JSON). (c) For Fig. views and Table III 'ale', report AUSE on defined pixels with the defined share next to it.

findings.title: CSS gets the classes present in the evaluation frames' GT, but the paper and baselines.py docstrings say it gets the full vocabulary
findings.where: papers/main.tex:643-644 (setup, 'Segmentation baselines'); usplat/baselines.py:33-37 (docstring (d)) and :336-337 (CSS.__init__ docstring); scripts/run_mapping.py:104-120 (css_vocabulary) and 228-230; scripts/replica_tab1.sh (--css-eval-data $ROOT/$s/Sequence_2)
findings.problem: run_mapping.css_vocabulary reads the label maps of the scene's evaluation sequence (Sequence_2, stride 10) at mapping time and builds the CSS Dirichlet over exactly the classes present there: 16-28 of 101. The paper says 'CSS receives the full vocabulary at mapping time, which the open-vocabulary rows do not need'; the baselines.py docstring says CSS gets 'configs/vocab_replica.json, all classes ... never the classes present in a test scene'. Both are false (the paper is true only if 'vocabulary' means the scene's query vocabulary, line 595). CSS has the same class information as other rows, only earlier. K also sets the strength of CSS's flat Dirichlet prior (see F05), so the stated protocol would give different CSS numbers.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader or reviewer believes CSS votes among 101 classes and credits its calibration (val ECE 4.65 vs 7.05 for ours P2) to a harder full-vocabulary setting it never ran. If the authors decide after the test run that CSS should get the full vocabulary, they must re-map and re-evaluate the test scenes (CSS counts are built at mapping time), i.e. a second test run. The comparison is otherwise fair and there is no crash risk in CSS.columns.
findings.evidence: CPU check (scratchpad/present.py) comparing css_vocabulary() with eval_seg's present-query rule (load_frames + torch.unique, downscale 2) for all 8 scenes: office_0 24/24, room_2 21/21, room_0 28/28, room_1 24/24, office_1 22/22, office_2 21/21, office_3 26/26, office_4 16/16; identical ids and order, no CSS-only class, 0 unknown label pixels. torch.load(office_0_lseg.pt)['css_class_ids'] = [10, 12, 17, 20, 22, 31, 35, 37, 40, 44, 47, 56, 60, 63, 76, 79, 80, 82, 83, 87, 92, 93, 95, 98] (24 of 101). map_office_0.log / stage_val.log: 'CSS vocabulary: 24 classes present in .../office_0/Sequence_2'; room_2 '21 classes'. The run report README line 17 says it correctly.
findings.fix: Decide before STAGE=test. Cheap option: keep the code and fix the text, e.g. main.tex:643-644: 'CSS receives at mapping time the classes present in the scene's evaluation frames (16 to 28 classes), the same set every row is queried with; the open-vocabulary rows need these classes only at query time.' Fix baselines.py docstring (d) and the CSS.__init__ docstring to match run_mapping. Only if a full-vocabulary CSS is wanted: change css_vocabulary to use all non-ignored vocab ids, re-map the val scenes and refit val betas before any test run.

findings.title: CSS's flat prior alpha0 = 1 is unstated and untuned, yet it is about 26-28% of the mass-weighted Dirichlet mean and likely drives CSS's ECE lead
findings.where: usplat/baselines.py:334-339 (alpha0=1.0, docstring '[A: fixed on val]'); usplat/baselines.py:526 (default_baselines alpha0=1.0); papers/main.tex:641-646
findings.problem: CSS's row buffer is (counts + alpha0)/(sum counts + K*alpha0). Counts are pixel masses at 240x320 and most Gaussians are tiny (median 4.2 px in office_0, 1.5 px in room_2), so the flat prior K*alpha0 is large next to the evidence, giving strong evidence-dependent smoothing toward uniform. That plausibly explains CSS's val calibration lead. It is a real property, not a bug (tie rule, coverage, temperature fit and class-column selection were checked and treat rows alike), but its size is set by three unstated choices: alpha0 = 1, K = number of present classes, and the mapping resolution. The '[A: fixed on val]' tag is not backed by any val selection.
findings.failure_scenario: The paper reports CSS as best-calibrated, or explains why P1/P2 lose on ECE/NLL, without saying the CSS predictive is ~27% uniform prior by mass. The CSS row cannot be reproduced since neither alpha0 nor K is given. With K = 101 as the paper describes, the prior share roughly doubles, so the stated setup would give a different CSS ECE.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/css_state.py on saved val fields: office_0 K 24 alpha0 1.0; CSS mass quantiles q10..q99 = [0.15, 0.72, 4.18, 20.2, 59.1, 256]; mass-weighted prior share 0.278, with K=101 0.533; CSS total counts = NormLift S1 (max abs diff 1e-3). room_2 K 21: 0.258, K=101 0.505. logs/eval_val_partial_2013.log: css ECE 0.0465 NLL 0.9563, beta 1.32; averaging ECE 0.0740 NLL 1.0653; ours_P2 ECE 0.0705 NLL 1.0549. grep -rn alpha0 over docs/reports/2026-09-29-data-and-baselines/, fact_sheet.md and papers/main.tex returns nothing.
findings.fix: State in the setup: 'CSS uses a flat Dirichlet prior, alpha_0 = 1 per class, over the K present classes, with counts in pixels at 240x320.' Replace '[A: fixed on val]' with 'default, not tuned'. Optionally pick alpha0 on val with a small grid (0.01, 0.1, 1) before the test run; it enters only at read-out, so no re-mapping is needed. When interpreting results, say CSS calibration comes from probability averaging plus prior smoothing.

findings.title: Stage guards only check that eval_val.json exists; the file on disk is a failed record with no betas, and eval_seg only warns
findings.where: scripts/replica_tab1.sh:29-46 (test maps built first), 56 (existence check); scripts/replica_views.sh:27; scripts/replica_tab3.sh:49, 125; scripts/eval_seg.py:474-478 (load_betas), 488-493 (check_fit_settings warns on None), 425 (betas_used raises only after load_scene); usplat/runlog.py
findings.problem: '[ -f "$OUT/eval_val.json" ]' accepts any record, including status 'running' (written at start) or 'failed' (metrics {}). In replica_tab1.sh the check runs after the loop that fits and maps all 6 test scenes. With an empty betas file, load_betas returns {} and check_fit_settings only warns; eval_seg then loads the first test scene (LSeg tokens, all rows frozen) and only then crashes in betas_used. A status 'ok' record from older code would also pass: the commit is not compared.
findings.failure_scenario: If STAGE=test is launched now, or after a crashed val rerun, the script spends hours of GPU time and ~8 GB of disk mapping test scenes (or k-view fields), then crashes on room_0 with 'rows [...] have no usable fitted beta'. No test metric leaks, but a failed test run is on record and the test maps are built from whatever code is checked out.
findings.evidence: /home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/data/uags_results/tab1/eval_val.json: status 'failed', start 20:13:45, end 20:16:30, metrics keys [] (OOM at 20:16:31). python3 (CPU) es.load_betas / load_fit_settings / check_fit_settings on it -> 'betas: {}', 'settings: None', UserWarning 'no beta_fit_settings recorded', 'check_fit_settings passed (warning only)'. Simulated failed RunRecord gives the same. replica_tab1.sh:56: [ -f "$OUT/eval_val.json" ] || { echo "run STAGE=val first"; exit 1; }; replica_views.sh:27 and replica_tab3.sh use the same existence-only check.
findings.fix: Move the check to the top of the test branch, before mapping, and replace it with a python3 -c json check: status == 'ok' (plain-json files have no status), metrics.betas holds every Table I row (ours_P0/P1/P2, ours_scalar, averaging, normlift, viewcount, css, 2d_features), and beta_fit_settings present. Apply in replica_tab1.sh, replica_views.sh and replica_tab3.sh. In eval_seg.run, raise instead of warn when --betas gives an empty dict or no beta_fit_settings.

findings.title: eval_seg.py saves no metrics until every scene is done, so a mid-run crash loses finished scenes and forces a second test pass
findings.where: scripts/eval_seg.py:540-554 (run: rec.add only after the scene loop); scripts/eval_seg.py:544-548 (per-scene print has no Brier/AURC/AUSE)
findings.problem: Per-scene results stay in memory; RunRecord gets them only after all scenes (for k, v in out.items(): rec.add(k, v)). If scene k crashes, scenes 1..k-1 are gone from the JSON and survive only as printed lines (mIoU/acc/ECE/NLL/coverage only) in a log the next launch overwrites.
findings.failure_scenario: The val eval already crashed twice with CUDA OOM on the shared GPU (15:18 and 20:16). If the test eval crashes on a later scene (e.g. office_2 or office_4 when a USGLoc job starts), the finished scenes' numbers have been printed and seen but Brier, AURC and AUSE_u are lost, and eval_test.json has metrics {}. The rerun must evaluate them again, breaking the run-test-once rule.
findings.evidence: eval_seg.py:541-549 fills res in memory; rec.add runs only at lines 551-553. RunRecord supports flush() but eval_seg never calls it per scene. The 20:13 val run finished office_0 then OOMed on room_2 (stage_val.log: 'torch.OutOfMemoryError ... frozen_on ... share', 'exit 1 2026-09-29 20:16:31'); python3 -c json load of tab1/eval_val.json -> metrics dict_keys([]); office_0 numbers had to be rebuilt from a transcript in logs/eval_val_partial_2013.log.
findings.fix: After each scene: rec.add('scenes', res) (or rec.add(f"scene_{name}", ...) / write <out>.<scene>.json); rec.add('betas', out['betas']); rec.flush(). Add --resume <partial.json> / --skip-done that loads finished scenes only if betas, beta_fit_settings, config_sha256 and git code hash all match, and evaluates only the missing scenes. Record in the report which scenes were resumed.

findings.title: A rerun destroys earlier results: logs and JSON are overwritten, and nothing stops a second STAGE=test
findings.where: scripts/replica_tab1.sh:53, 56-59; usplat/runlog.py:682-715 (RunRecord.__enter__ calls flush()); scripts/eval_seg.py:609-612
findings.problem: The shell '> $OUT/eval_<stage>.log' empties the log as soon as gpu_gate.sh starts, before the gate lets the job run. RunRecord writes the --out JSON with status 'running' at start, replacing the old eval_val.json or eval_test.json at once. Nothing checks for an existing eval_test.json before the test branch runs.
findings.failure_scenario: The first test run writes eval_test.json with status ok. A mistaken or 'retry' relaunch of STAGE=test empties eval_test.log and turns eval_test.json into a 'running' record with metrics {}. The only copy of the test numbers is gone and recovery needs a second test run. This already happened on val: the 20:18:31 relaunch overwrote eval_val.log, and office_0 numbers survive only as a hand copy.
findings.evidence: replica_tab1.sh:59 '--out "$OUT/eval_test.json" > "$OUT/eval_test.log" 2>&1'. Simulated RunRecord: file has status 'running' inside the with-block and ends 'failed' with metrics {}. tab1/eval_val.log starts at '[gpu_gate] 2026-09-29 20:18:31 waiting' and holds only 84 KB of gate lines. stage_val.log line 125: 'restart 2026-09-29 20:18:31 at cc65f08'.
findings.fix: (1) Per-launch logs: TAG=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S); write eval_${STAGE}_${TAG}.log and ln -sf eval_${STAGE}.log, or append with >> after a header (date, git rev-parse HEAD, env). (2) In the test branch, refuse if eval_test.json exists unless FORCE_TEST_RERUN=<reason> is set and logged. (3) In eval_seg.main, refuse an --out holding a record with status ok or running unless --overwrite, or write to <out>.<run_id>.json and copy to --out only on success.

findings.title: Mapping does not use 180 frames: the near-duplicate pose filter keeps 176-180 per scene (and fewer for k-view fields); 3D-GS map fit on 157
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:183-200 (select, defaults --kf-trans 0.05 --kf-rot 5); scripts/replica_tab1.sh:37-40 (no kf flags); papers/main.tex:593, 616-617, 693, 768-775 (Setup 'every 5th frame of Sequence_1 (180 frames)', fig:views 'M of the 180 mapping frames', M in {10,30,90,180})
findings.problem: select() drops a frame whose pose is within 5 cm AND 5 deg of the last kept frame, applied after the evenly spaced subset. Every scene but one loses 1-4 of its 180 frames, and k-view budgets are not always exact. The paper does not mention the filter. The 3D-GS geometry is also fit on 157 of 180 frames (every 8th held out for PSNR), while the text says it is fit 'on the mapping frames'.
findings.failure_scenario: The setup text and views figure axis state frame counts the pipeline does not use: office_1's field uses 176 frames, room_1's 90-frame field uses 89, 'M=180' is really 176-180. A reproduction with all 180 frames gives slightly different fields. All rows share the same frames, so the comparison stays fair.
findings.evidence: Replaying select()/_pose_gap on traj_w_c.txt in float32 (scratchpad/kf_select.py and inline): office_0 179, room_2 179, room_0 179, room_1 178, office_1 176, office_2 178, office_3 179, office_4 180. Example: office_0 frame 295 dropped (3.2 cm, 2.6 deg). k=10 and k=30 exact for all 8 scenes; room_1 budgets {10:10, 30:30, 90:89, 180:178}. Map logs: 'keyframes used 179' for office_0 and room_2. fit_room_2.log meta: n_train 157, n_test 23; map meta holdout_every 8.
findings.fix: Cheapest: change the text, e.g. 'every 5th frame of Sequence_1 (180 frames; near-duplicate poses, <5 cm and <5 deg from the previous kept frame, are skipped: 176-180 per scene)', 'the full map (all kept frames)', and say the 3D-GS map is fit on 157 of them (every 8th held out). For the figure, subsample after the filter so k is exact, or plot the recorded n_mapping_views. Alternative: pass --kf-trans 0 --kf-rot 0 in replica_tab1.sh and replica_views.sh, but then both val fields must be rebuilt and betas refit before the test run.

findings.title: PCA centre sample pins about 3 GiB of GPU memory for the whole mapping run
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:162-174 (raw.append at 168, never deleted); same code at 60d7796:167
findings.problem: raw.append(z.reshape(-1, clip.d)[::step]) stores a strided VIEW that keeps each full per-frame buffer alive: 240x320x512 fp32 = 150 MiB, so 20 x 150 = 3000 MiB for 200 MiB of samples. The list stays alive on the GPU through token extraction and the whole mapping pass, though it is dead after the centre is computed at lines 170-172.
findings.failure_scenario: The office_0 mapping peak of 4807 MiB is ~3000 MiB dead PCA buffers plus ~1.8 GiB real work. If 'Peak GPU memory is \ph GB' (main.tex:951) is filled from peak_alloc_mib, the paper overstates memory by ~2.9 GiB. README root causes are wrong: 'LSeg needs > 3.3 GB at the first PCA frame' (LSeg weights 1554 MiB, activations <= 334 MiB, so the 14:20 probe likely failed near the 9th-10th PCA frame), and 'mapping memory grows with N' misses a fixed ~3 GiB. MAP_NEED=9000 (+2048 headroom = 11 GB free) is sized around the leak, so the test stage waits for large USGLoc gaps for no reason.
findings.evidence: 1) CPU run of the real code path (scratchpad/raw_probe.py, fake extractor, downscale 2, pca-frames 20): 'RAW: 20 frames, 200 MiB of samples keep 3000 MiB alive'. 2) upsample_tokens((60,80,512)->(240,320)) then reshape(-1,512)[::15]: 'storage kept alive 150.0 MiB' for 'raw bytes needed 10.0 MiB'. 3) Mapping peak 4806 MiB with 3 keyframes (logs/smoke_mapping_3kf.log) and 4807 MiB with 179 (map_office_0.log); room_2 (954,119 G) 5732 vs office_0 (620,290 G) 4807 -> 2.9 KB/Gaussian, leaving an N-independent ~3.09 GiB. 4) LSeg on CPU: 'LSeg net MiB 1311.8 | CLIP text MiB 242.0 | total 1553.7'.
findings.fix: After the centre loop (after line 174), add 'del raw, z'; this changes no saved value. To also cut the PCA-phase peak, store z.reshape(-1, clip.d)[::step].clone() (or .cpu()). Then re-measure mapping and extraction peaks and correct the README memory findings and the MAP_NEED cap.

findings.title: GPU reservation makes peak_alloc_extract_mib and peak_reserved_mib report the reservation, not the job
findings.where: usplat/gpu_reserve.py:31-33; scripts/run_mapping.py:232-233, 281-282, 312-317; scripts/eval_seg.py:519-523 with usplat/runlog.py memory peaks
findings.problem: apply() allocates one tensor of cap-512 MiB and frees it. torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() counts it, and nothing resets the peak before run_mapping.py:232 reads it. The reset at line 282 sets the reserved peak to current reserved memory, which includes the cached block. Both fields hold the reservation size from commit cc65f08 on.
findings.failure_scenario: MAP_NEED=9000 -> cap 8739 MiB -> reservation 8227 MiB. Every test-scene map log will show peak_alloc_extract_mib and peak_reserved_mib >= 8227, where val logs (5b21781, no reservation) show 4914/5354 and 4931/6456. A paper peak-memory number or report memory table taken from these fields would be the gate's cap, not the method. eval_seg's RunRecord 'memory' peaks are inflated the same way.
findings.evidence: gpu_reserve.py:31 'block = torch.empty(mib * 2 ** 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)', run before load_gaussians (run_mapping.py:142-143); no reset_peak_memory_stats before line 232. Cap arithmetic confirmed by OOM messages: cap 6000 -> '5.69 GiB allowed', cap 3500 -> '3.32 GiB allowed'. map_office_0.log: 'peak_alloc_extract_mib': 4914.41..., 'peak_reserved_mib': 5354.0. No GPU run with the reservation exists yet (stage_val.log: cc65f08 restart still queued when stopped at 21:53).
findings.fix: At the end of apply(), after 'del block', call torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(device). Save the reservation size in the timing dict and mark peak_reserved_mib as not meaningful while a reservation is held. For the paper's timing run, use UAGS_GPU_RESERVE=0 on an idle GPU.

findings.title: Timing fields cannot fill the paper's run-time breakdown and overstate our per-keyframe cost
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:206-213, 259-277, 307-317; papers/main.tex:946-955
findings.problem: The paper promises total ms, LSeg extraction ms, render+backward ms, and statistics/change test/re-admission ms; the code gives three fields. (a) update_view is timed as one block, so render+backward is not split from the statistics. (b) ms_per_keyframe_field includes view-hook baselines (NormLift/averaging and view count run inside update_view, vmf_field.py:323,352). (c) Since 5b21781, ms_per_keyframe_extract times extract_tokens plus D2H only; H2D, upsample, normalisation, PCA projection (line 261), rasterizer setup (262-264) and gaussian_depths are timed nowhere, so extract + update is not the total. (d) Means include the first-call warm-up; usplat.runlog.Timer drops warm-up, this code does not.
findings.failure_scenario: If filled from the Tab I map logs, 'render and backward' and 'total' include the three baselines' hook work, and the total omits upsample/PCA/raster setup. The paper would state per-part times that were never measured.
findings.evidence: Smoke log (3 keyframes): ms_per_keyframe_field 123.96 vs 29.82 at 179 keyframes (map_office_0.log), so the first call costs ~312 ms and adds ~1.6 ms (~5%) to the 179-frame mean. office_0: update 40.3, field 29.8, extract 65.9 ms. No timers inside vmf_field/bki_accumulate (grep of time/Timer/perf_counter). Old code (60d7796:219-223) timed extractor + upsample + PCA as 'extract'; new comment says 'extractor (tokens) only'.
findings.fix: For the timing run: map one validation scene without --baselines (or time hooks separately); add synchronised timers inside update_view around render+backward (bki accumulate) and around statistics/change test; time upsample+PCA+H2D and rasterizer setup and report the sum as total; drop the first keyframe (or use runlog.Timer with warm-up). Use UAGS_GPU_RESERVE=0 and fix the raw leak (F10) first.

findings.title: Field files carry no code version, and existing fields are reused without a check, so val and test fields can come from different code
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:319-323 (saved dict has no git/code hash); scripts/replica_tab1.sh:36 (reuse if the file exists); scripts/eval_seg.py:247-251 (checks only extractor name); usplat/extractors/lseg.py:293-307 (UAGS_LSEG_STRIDE/FLIP/SCALES/HALF env overrides, not recorded)
findings.problem: Temperatures are fit on val fields (office_0 built at 5b21781, room_2 at 5e8c51e). Test fields will be built later from whatever code is checked out, while attempt 06 (P3) is being implemented. Nothing records or compares mapping code, FieldConfig defaults or LSeg options between the sets; eval_seg compares only the extractor name. fit_gs.py records git and code_sha256 in its map meta; run_mapping does not.
findings.failure_scenario: If P3 or any fix changes vmf_field/baselines/FieldConfig defaults before STAGE=test, test fields carry different statistics from the val fields the betas were fit on, and Table I mixes two methods with no trace in any file. The same happens silently if UAGS_LSEG_* or DOWNSCALE differ in the test shell.
findings.evidence: torch.load(..._lseg.pt, mmap=True) keys: ['baselines','config','css_class_ids','extractor','field','field_config','pca','timing'], no git entry. Val configs differ only in paths; field_config identical. git diff 5b21781 HEAD --stat -- usplat scripts shows only run_mapping/gpu_reserve changes, so the sets still match today. Map meta shows office_0 git '408dc8a+dirty' and room_2 '260afb7' with code_sha256.
findings.fix: In run_mapping, save code=usplat.runlog.git_state(...) (commit, dirty, code_sha256) plus LSeg options (token_stride, flip, scales, half) in the field file. In eval_seg.load_scene collect these per scene; in --betas mode refuse when a test field's code hash or config (minus paths) differs from the fields named in the betas record, which must store its fields' hashes in beta_fit_settings. Minimum: replica_tab1.sh STAGE=test prints git rev-parse HEAD and git status --short into the stage log and refuses a dirty tree.

findings.title: The std in the tables is the population std (ddof=0); the paper says only 'standard deviation'
findings.where: usplat/seg_eval.py:613-621 (scene_stats, v.std(unbiased=False)); papers/main.tex:623-624, 726; scripts/make_tables.py:47-53
findings.problem: summarize_scenes and make_tables report the population std over N=6 scenes. Most readers assume the sample std (ddof=1), which is sqrt(6/5) = 1.095 times larger, so every +- in Tables I and III and Fig. views reads about 9% smaller than expected.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer computes the std from per-scene numbers with the usual sample formula and gets values about 9.5% larger than the table shows.
findings.evidence: seg_eval.py:620: std=float(v.std(unbiased=False)); main.tex:623: 'We report the mean and standard deviation over the test scenes (N=6 ...)'.
findings.fix: Either use unbiased=True (std is computed from saved per-scene numbers, so the test run is unaffected) or write 'population standard deviation' in the setup text. Also consider stating the AUSE grid size (20 fractions) in the metrics paragraph.

findings.title: Paper says tau_cov is set on the validation scenes, but it is a fixed default (0.5)
findings.where: papers/main.tex:621-622; scripts/replica_tab1.sh:21 (TAU_COV=${TAU_COV:-0.5}); scripts/eval_seg.py:563-564 (help '[A: set on Replica val]'); usplat/seg_eval.py:29 (docstring 'COVERAGE RULE (plan §3, fixed before any val run)')
findings.problem: The text says 'The coverage floor tau_cov=\ph and all temperatures are set on the validation scenes.' No script or report selects tau_cov on validation; it defaults to 0.5 in all three pipeline scripts, and seg_eval.py calls the rule 'fixed before any val run'.
findings.failure_scenario: The paper claims a validation choice that was never made; a reviewer asking how tau_cov was tuned gets no run or log. No leak, since the value is fixed.
findings.evidence: grep over docs/reports and scripts/*.sh: tau_cov appears only as TAU_COV=${TAU_COV:-0.5} in replica_tab1.sh, replica_tab3.sh and replica_views.sh plus the plan symbol list. No selection run.
findings.fix: Write 'tau_cov = 0.5, fixed before any run; all temperatures are fit on the validation scenes', and fix the --tau-cov help text.

findings.title: Output record lists the wrong prompt templates for the LSeg run
findings.where: scripts/eval_seg.py:525-526 (out['vocab']['templates']); scripts/eval_seg.py:103-107, 134
findings.problem: out['vocab']['templates'] is vocab['templates'], which load_vocab builds from the legacy 'template' key: the single ClearCLIP template 'a photo of a {} in a room.'. The text embeddings actually come from extractor_templates(vocab, 'lseg'), the 5-template LSeg ensemble. Provenance in eval_val.json and eval_test.json misstates the prompts behind every Table I number.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader or later script takes eval_test.json's vocab.templates as the prompts used and sees one ClearCLIP template, not the frozen 5-template ensemble; the run cannot be reproduced from the record alone.
findings.evidence: CPU check: load_vocab('configs/vocab_replica.json')['templates'] -> ['a photo of a {} in a room.']; extractor_templates(v,'lseg') -> ['a photo of a {}.', 'a photo of the {}.', 'there is a {} in the scene.', 'a photo of a {} in a room.', 'a cropped photo of a {}.'].
findings.fix: Record templates=extractor_templates(vocab, args.extractor), plus the extractor name, in out['vocab']. Optionally hash the text tensor used.

findings.title: The 'never beside USGLoc' gate policy lives only in an unrecorded environment variable; gate comments are stale
findings.where: scripts/gpu_gate.sh:8-10, 14, 21, 40-44 (UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB default 0); scripts/replica_tab1.sh, replica_views.sh, replica_tab3.sh (no gate env pinned)
findings.problem: The README and stage_val.log say the val restart ran 'never beside a USGLoc job', and the 20:18 relaunch waited for free >= 109047 MiB, but the gate's default extra is 0 (requirement 9000 + 2048 = 11048 MiB) and its header still says parallel runs are allowed. The policy came from a hand-set env var that no script or log records. Line 14 still says run_mapping uses set_per_process_memory_fraction; it now goes through gpu_reserve, and the cap is 0.971 x need (9000 -> 8739 MiB). TAU_COV and DOWNSCALE overrides are also not pinned; a tau_cov mismatch only warns.
findings.failure_scenario: STAGE=test launched from a fresh shell uses a different gate policy from val and may start beside a running USGLoc job, the setup of the 15:18 and 20:16 eval OOMs. Numbers stay deterministic, but the run can crash, and test map ms/keyframe are taken on a shared GPU. gpu_reserve lowers the risk.
findings.evidence: gpu_gate.sh:21 'usgloc_extra=${UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB:-0}'; required() = need + headroom (+ usgloc_extra if USGLoc running). tab1/eval_val.log: '[gpu_gate] 2026-09-29 20:18:31 waiting: free 590 MiB < 109047 or lock busy'. stage_val.log: 'restart 2026-09-29 20:18:31 at cc65f08 (poll 5 s, never beside a USGLoc job, memory reserved at start)'. OOM texts: 6000 -> '5.69 GiB allowed'.
findings.fix: Pin the policy in replica_tab1.sh/replica_views.sh/replica_tab3.sh (export UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB=${UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB:-99999}) or change the gate default. Echo all UAGS_* vars, TAU_COV and DOWNSCALE into the stage log at start and record the launch env in the report. Make eval_seg refuse, not warn, when tau_cov differs from the fit's value. Update gate comments at lines 8-14.

findings.title: run_mapping sets no seed, so PCA bases differ between fits (k-view fields add basis noise to e_red / e_irr)
findings.where: usplat/feature_pca.py:32-34 (torch.randperm on z.device); scripts/run_mapping.py:129-173 (no torch.manual_seed in run_gsplat), 161-169; scripts/replica_views.sh:35-39
findings.problem: Each PCA frame (76,800 pixels) is cut to 20,000 random pixels. run_gsplat never seeds, so the basis is reproducible only if the CUDA default generator starts from a fixed seed and no earlier CUDA random call moved it; the CPU default seed is random per process. Each k-view field fits its own PCA on the same 20 frames with an unseeded subsample. eval_views stays internally consistent (each field projects text with its own basis, eval_seg.py:256,281), but a pixel can flip right/wrong from the basis alone and is then counted as e_red or dropped from e_irr.
findings.failure_scenario: The same saved command rebuilds a field with a slightly different basis, so fields are not reproducible by construction. A small share of e_red / e_irr pixels comes from PCA sampling noise, not the number of views; this matters most at k=90, where e_red is smallest.
findings.evidence: Two CPU runs of torch.initial_seed(), torch.randperm(76800)[:3]: 5031214125354848027 [51648, 24706, 34024] and 5751053207044270839 [29599, 29431, 32253]. grep finds no manual_seed in run_mapping.run_gsplat (CUDA default not checked: no GPU use allowed). CPU proxy (scratchpad/pca_seed_effect.py, OpenCLIP tokens): labels changed on 0.141% (office_0) and 0.111% (room_2) of pixels between two fits; correctness flipped on 0.073% / 0.069%.
findings.fix: Add torch.manual_seed(args.seed) (new --seed, default 0) at the start of run_gsplat, or pass a torch.Generator to StreamingPCA.accumulate, and store the seed in the field file. Map the k-view fields with the full field's basis (--pca-from, see F01) and assert in eval_views that k-field and full-field bases are equal.

findings.title: make_tables.py does not match the tab:replica layout and does not check its input
findings.where: scripts/make_tables.py:20-29, 48-66; papers/main.tex tab:replica (\midrule before Ours, P2 row with \multicolumn{2}{c}{as P0})
findings.problem: (a) No \midrule between CSS and Ours P0. (b) For Ours P2 it prints mIoU and Acc numbers, but the paper has \multicolumn{2}{c}{as P0}. (c) It prints 'same predictive as averaging' for both NormLift rows without checking the metrics are equal. (d) std is population std (scene_stats unbiased=False), unstated; N appears only in a comment as a set over rows, so a cell with fewer scenes (NaN dropped) is not flagged. (e) It does not check the JSON is a finished test record and would print eval_val.json numbers (N=2) under the 'test, N=6' caption.
findings.failure_scenario: Generated rows cannot be pasted as-is (P2 row and midrule differ). If NormLift's buffer ever differs from averaging's, the table still claims the same predictive. Run on the wrong file, val numbers appear under the test caption.
findings.evidence: tab1() on a synthetic 6-scene summary (scratchpad fake_test.json): 8 rows in the right order and labels, no \midrule, and 'Ours P2 (adaptive $\beta$) & \checkmark & 44.0{...} & 32.8{...} & ...' with numbers in mIoU/Acc cells. Units correct: mIoU/Acc/ECE/AURC/AUSE x100 1 decimal, Brier x100, NLL 2 decimals. seg_eval.py:613-621 uses population std.
findings.fix: Emit '\midrule' before the first Ours row. For ours_P2, assert |mIoU/Acc(P2) - mIoU/Acc(P0)| < 1e-9 per scene and print '\multicolumn{2}{c}{as P0}'. For NormLift rows, assert the predictive summary equals averaging's, else raise. Assert status == 'ok', 'betas_path' present (not a fit), and summary n == 6 for every printed cell. Write 'std over scenes (population), N = 6' in the caption.

findings.title: Tab III 'Full method' temperatures will differ from Tab I 'Ours' because the 2D row shifts the fitter's random subsets
findings.where: scripts/eval_seg.py:390-400 (fit_on adds rows2d between scenes); usplat/seg_eval.py:446,466-469 (one seeded generator shared by all add calls); scripts/replica_tab1.sh:49 (--with-2d) vs scripts/replica_tab3.sh:118-120 (no --with-2d)
findings.problem: BetaFitter draws the per-view pixel subset (cap 2000) from one generator. In Tab I the 2D row's office_0 views draw from it before room_2's 3D rows are added, so room_2 gets different subsets than in the Tab III fit, which has no 2D row. The ours_* betas depend on whether an unrelated row is present.
findings.failure_scenario: In Tab III, 'Full method' ECE/NLL (and P2 parameters) will not match the Ours row of Tab I for the same field; a reader sees two different numbers for one method.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/beta_2d_shift.py (toy CLI, two val scenes, --fit-pixels 50): ours_P0 beta 8.520 with the 2D row vs 9.826 without; P2 beta0 45.74 vs 36.51. With the real cap of 2000 the shift will be smaller but not zero.
findings.fix: Seed the subset per (scene, view), e.g. a generator seeded from hash(scene name, frame idx), or fit the 2D row with its own BetaFitter, or have Tab III reuse the Tab I betas for the ours_* rows.

findings.title: Ablation rows exist only for P0 and P2, but the paper leaves the full method's predictive open (P0, P1 or P2)
findings.where: usplat/ablation_rows.py:65-70; papers/main.tex sec:ablation ('The full method uses \todo{the predictive chosen on validation (P0, P1 or P2 ...)}')
findings.problem: variant_rows builds abl_<v>_P0 and abl_<v>_P2 (P2 on the P0 buffer) only.
findings.failure_scenario: If validation picks P1 (best office_0 mIoU in the partial log, 0.3011), the Tab III variant rows cannot use the same predictive as the Full row, so each row would change two things.
findings.evidence: eval_val_partial_2013.log: ours_P1 mIoU 0.3011 vs P0/P2 0.3002; P2 has the best ECE/NLL.
findings.fix: Fix the choice (P2) in the text now, or add abl_<v>_P1 rows (FieldRow mode='P1') before the Tab III val fit.

findings.title: The 2D row covers every pixel, while the 3D rows count their uncovered pixels as wrong; the paper does not say this
findings.where: scripts/eval_seg.py:359-371 (PixelSource returns alpha = 1); papers/main.tex:628-629 and 679-682
findings.problem: The 2D row's rasterizer returns alpha = 1 for every pixel, so all labelled pixels count as covered. The 3D rows lose about 0.3% of pixels to the coverage rule; those count as wrong and get the uniform predictive in the 'all' variant. The metrics text defines coverage through 'rendered opacity', which the 2D row lacks.
findings.failure_scenario: The 2D vs 3D accuracy gap in Table I includes up to ~0.3 points from coverage, not semantics. Small but unstated.
findings.evidence: eval_val_partial_2013.log: office_0 2d_features coverage 1.000; all 3D rows coverage 0.997.
findings.fix: Add to the setup: '2D features cover every pixel; a 3D row's pixels with alpha_p < tau_cov count as wrong (0.3% on validation)'. Or also report the 'covered' variant for the 3D rows.

findings.title: The views figure's M=180 point (e_irr column) is not produced by replica_views.sh
findings.where: scripts/replica_views.sh:18 (KS='10 30 90'); papers/main.tex fig:views placeholder ('plus M=180 in the e_irr column')
findings.problem: The pipeline makes no 180 point. At M=180, e_irr equals the 0/1 error on covered pixels, so the value equals the Tab I eval JSON summary[row]['covered']['ause'][channel] (same pixel set, same three-tier key). Nothing documents or extracts it.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever draws the figure must find the M=180 value by hand, or map a duplicate 'k=180' field for no reason.
findings.evidence: seg_eval.summarize (covered variant, err = 1 - correct, ranking_signals on covered pixels) and views_cross_ause (covered in both maps, identical geometry) select the same pixels and keys.
findings.fix: Take the M=180 point from the Tab I test JSON ('covered' variant) in the figure script, and note this in the eval_views docstring.

findings.title: Field and map saves are not atomic and have no disk check, so a truncated file would be reused
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:323 (torch.save(out, args.out)); usplat/gs_fit.py:708; scripts/replica_tab1.sh:30, 36 (reuse if the file exists); scripts/replica_tab3.sh:34-38
findings.problem: The disk is 97% full (30 GB free) and shared with USGLoc. If torch.save fails or is killed part-way, a partial .pt stays at the final path; the next run skips mapping ('file exists') and eval_seg crashes on torch.load. In replica_tab3.sh:34-38, a failed mapping call ends the script under set -e before the log tail is printed.
findings.failure_scenario: If USGLoc fills the disk while office_3's 1.3 GB field is written, the test eval crashes on a truncated file, and the fix and rerun also re-evaluate scenes already done (see F07).
findings.evidence: df: /dev/nvme0n1p1 937G, 861G used, 30G avail (97%). Field size ~1.3 kB per Gaussian (office_0 819,126,064 B / 620,290; room_2 1,236,880,094 B / 954,119), up to 1.32 GB per field at the 1M cap. Table I test needs <= ~8.3 GB (6 fields + ~56 MB maps); Table III variants and views fields share the disk.
findings.fix: Save to args.out + '.tmp' then os.replace. Before each mapping call check df --output=avail >= 3 GB and stop with a message if not. In replica_tab3.sh:34 add '|| { tail -20 log; exit 1; }' to the gpu_gate call itself.

findings.title: replica_tab3.sh hides the mapping log when a variant mapping fails
findings.where: scripts/replica_tab3.sh:110-114
findings.problem: Under set -e, a failing gpu_gate/run_mapping command at line 110 ends the script at once. The '|| { tail ...; }' is attached to the grep on line 114, not to the mapping command, unlike replica_tab1.sh and replica_views.sh.
findings.failure_scenario: An OOM or crash while mapping a variant exits with no message on the console.
findings.evidence: Lines 110-113 have no '||' after the redirect.
findings.fix: Append '|| { tail -20 "$OUT/map_${s}_${v}.log"; exit 1; }' to the gpu_gate command.

findings.title: STAGE is not validated, so any value other than 'val' runs the test branch
findings.where: scripts/replica_tab1.sh:27, 50 (if [ "$STAGE" = val ] ... else <test>); same pattern in replica_tab3.sh and replica_views.sh
findings.problem: Both branches test only for the literal 'val'. A typo or another word ('Val', 'validation', 'tset') selects the test scenes and the test evaluation.
findings.failure_scenario: After a successful val run, 'STAGE=Val scripts/replica_tab1.sh' (meant as a val rerun) maps the 6 test scenes and runs the one-time test evaluation.
findings.evidence: bash check: STAGE=val -> val scenes; STAGE=Val, test, tset -> 'TEST scenes + test eval'.
findings.fix: At the top: case "$STAGE" in val|test) ;; *) echo "STAGE must be val or test"; exit 1;; esac. For test, also require an explicit CONFIRM_TEST=1.

findings.title: A failed reservation crashes a job that would otherwise fit
findings.where: usplat/gpu_reserve.py:31; scripts/gpu_gate.sh:35
findings.problem: The reservation (cap-512 = 8227 MiB for a 9000 cap) is much larger than the job's real peak (4.8-5.7 GiB, ~2-3 GiB after the raw fix). torch.empty is not guarded. The gate checks free memory seconds before python reaches apply(); if another process takes memory in that window, the job dies at start with OOM although its real need would fit.
findings.failure_scenario: The gate sees 11 GB free and starts the job. USGLoc's batch driver (bash batch_12s.sh, wait_gpu 7000/10000, 30 s poll) is not a python process, so the gate cannot see it; it launches train_locfeat during the ~5 s torch import. Free memory drops to ~7 GB, torch.empty(8227 MiB) raises, replica_tab1.sh exits 1. No test number is produced; it costs a restart.
findings.evidence: gpu_reserve.py:31 has no try/except. gpu_gate.sh:35 only matches 'pgrep -x python3|python'. Live USGLoc parent chain: 'bash .../batch_12s.sh cwd=/home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/src/usgloc' -> python3 run_7scenes.py.
findings.fix: Wrap the allocation in try/except torch.OutOfMemoryError; retry with half the size, or return 0 with a warning. The per-process cap still applies either way.

findings.title: frozen_on never shares channels that contain NaN (u_ale), unlike its docstring says
findings.where: scripts/eval_seg.py:294-306 (share uses torch.equal); tests/test_seg_eval.py:761-780
findings.problem: torch.equal returns False when a tensor has NaN. u_ale is NaN for undefined Gaussians (77-88% of Gaussians on the val maps), so each ours row keeps its own GPU copy. The test passes only because its toy field has no NaN. No number changes; it costs memory (~4 MB per copy per 1M Gaussians).
findings.failure_scenario: No wrong number. The docstring claim 'u_epi / u_ale of every ours row stored once' is false on real maps.
findings.evidence: CPU: torch.equal(tensor([1., nan]), same.clone()) -> False (torch 2.11.0+cu128). README support_stats: u_ale defined for 22.4% / 12.2% of Gaussians.
findings.fix: Compare with torch.equal(a.isnan(), b.isnan()) and torch.equal(a.nan_to_num(), b.nan_to_num()), or fix the docstring. Add NaN to the toy test.

findings.title: A stale LaTeX comment says normlift_1-Cinter is not exposed
findings.where: papers/main.tex:720-722
findings.problem: The comment says 'usplat/baselines.py defines c_inter() but uncertainties() exposes only normlift_1-R and normlift_epi. Expose normlift_1-Cinter before this row runs.' Commit 4829617 added that channel (baselines.py:246), and make_tables.py reads it.
findings.failure_scenario: A later editor or reviewer trusts the comment and thinks the 1 - C_inter row of Table I cannot have been measured.
findings.evidence: baselines.py:243-246 returns 'normlift_1-Cinter'; tests/test_baselines.py:147-149 checks it; on office_0 it is finite, range [-2.4e-7, 1.0].
findings.fix: Delete the three comment lines.

findings.title: Near-zero-evidence Gaussians: mu* is not unit and the support is 0 instead of W1
findings.where: usplat/vmf_field.py:613-614 (mu_post = F.normalize(kappa_hat*R), eps 1e-12); usplat/vmf_field.py:191-198 (kish() returns 0 when W2 < 1e-12, so support = min(0, W1) = 0)
findings.problem: The paper defines mu* = R/||R|| and s = W1. For Gaussians with W1 < ~3e-6, kappa_hat is clamped to 1e-6, so ||kappa_hat R|| < 1e-12 and F.normalize returns a vector shorter than 1 (min 0.17). W2 < 1e-12 makes kish = 0, so support = 0 and u_epi = 1 instead of 1/(1+W1).
findings.failure_scenario: No measurable effect on Table I (these Gaussians hold < 3e-11 of the pixel mass). It is a silent departure from the stated definitions and could matter for a map with many near-invisible Gaussians or a smaller a0.
findings.evidence: python3 scratchpad/field_stats.py office_0 room_2 -> office_0 'support < W1 (min binds): 1728; kish==0 while W1>0: 1728, their max W1 2.94e-06', 'P0 |mu*| on seen: min 0.1736 #(<0.999) 332'; room_2 '2729 ... max W1 2.99e-06', '#(<0.999) 579'. gate_share.py -> '|mu*|<0.999 on 332 seen Gaussians: max W1 1.25e-07, pixel-mass share 1.57e-11' (room_2: 579, 2.74e-11).
findings.fix: Compute mu* as R/||R|| (clamped) when prior_kappa = 0. In views mode, use support = W1, or compute kish with a relative epsilon (W2 > 0) instead of the absolute 1e-12.
